prompt: What is the name of the in-place, stable comparison sorting algorithm with a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and a best-case time complexity of O(n)?
answer:
The algorithm is **Timsort**—a stable, adaptive comparison sort with **O(n log n)** worst-case time and **O(n)** best-case time on already or nearly sorted data.

Strictly speaking, standard Timsort is **not fully in-place** because it uses auxiliary memory, typically **O(n)** in the worst case.
